failure_summary.description: The agent followed nearby context or a related entity instead of the clue’s requested category or relation, despite existing guidance to prioritize the exact wording.
The agent missed a requested appellation and a shared wordplay answer because the skill lacks explicit guidance for these clue forms.
The agent expanded an expected short title or surname into a longer canonical form.

patch.reasoning: The existing skill already covers technical categories, exact clue relations, and distractors, so those ignored rules should not be duplicated. Refine the answer-form guidance to distinguish appellations and established short forms from formal names, and add a focused rule for clues whose two readings point to one shared word.

edits.target: - Return one concise canonical answer at exactly the requested level of specificity. For fill-in or clue-style prompts, supply only the missing headword or name component; do not repeat information already given in the clue or add clue modifiers unless they are part of the canonical answer. For definition clues, give the requested category term rather than a list of examples, and match grammatical number and necessary articles. Use a full canonical personal name when the clue does not supply a name component; when it supplies part of a name and asks for completion, give only the missing component. Avoid explanations and alternatives.
edits.content: - Return one concise conventional answer in the form and at the level of specificity requested. For fill-in or clue-style prompts, supply only the missing headword or name component; do not repeat information already given or add modifiers unless they are part of the canonical answer. Use an established short form, surname, or abbreviated title when it is sufficient and supported by the clue or a direct source; expand to a full personal name or title only when needed to identify the referent or explicitly requested. If the clue asks what someone is called by others, give that appellation (such as a nickname, kinship label, title, or epithet), not the person's formal name. For definition clues, give the requested category term rather than a list of examples, and match grammatical number and necessary articles. Avoid explanations and alternatives.

- For wordplay or double-definition clues that offer two descriptions or readings of the same answer, look for the concise word or phrase that fits both readings. Return that shared answer rather than paraphrasing only one side.
